node.label: Thomas W. Laqueur
node.description: A cultural historian of the body, sexuality and death. Making Sex (1990) argues that a ‘one-sex’ model, in which men and women were thought to share the same basic body, gave way in the eighteenth century to a ‘two-sex’ model grounded in biological difference: sex difference itself has a history. The thesis has been both influential and contested. Brooke Holmes, drawing on work by Katharine Park, Robert Nye, Joan Cadden and Helen King, argues that the evidence shows more varied and coexisting models, and traces the book’s narrative of epochal rupture to Foucault’s history of sexuality. Caroline Walker Bynum drew on it while noting Park and Nye’s qualification. Solitary Sex (2003) is a cultural history of masturbation, and The Work of the Dead (2015) asks what the care and naming of the dead do for the living.
